name: hysteresis-latch
title: Hysteresis Latch
description: A switch whose two directions cost differently: a click or Space turns it ON instantly, but turning it OFF needs a drag past 85% of the track (or Space then a confirming Enter) — a faint SVG loop under the thumb ghosts the two coercive points so the asymmetry reads as physics, not a bug.
useWhen: a boolean setting where the two directions are not equally consequential — disabling 2FA, auto-backup, or prod write-protection — and the guard should live in the control's own drag/threshold physics rather than a bolted-on confirm dialog; pick switch-frost or switch-eclipse instead for an ordinary symmetric-threshold setting with no directional risk, or confirm-hold-ink when the risky action is a one-shot button rather than a toggle with a resting state.
instruction: Build a role=switch pill (84x36 track, 28px thumb, radius-full, border-border hairline, bg-background) whose ON and OFF transitions are asymmetric drag gestures rather than one symmetric threshold. A thin SVG (viewBox 0 0 100 40, preserveAspectRatio=none) sits under the thumb and draws two logistic curves in --ns-muted at 30% stroke-opacity, one inflecting at t=0.4 (the ON coercive point) and one at t=0.85 (the OFF coercive point) — purely decorative, but literally the same two fractions the drag math uses, so the loop explains the resistance instead of just prettifying it. Dragging from OFF maps pointer position to thumb position ~1:1 and commits ON the instant the drag crosses 40% of the 48px travel, then a short/light spring (k=260, zeta=0.78) finishes the slide to the end. Dragging from ON maps the pointer through a sub-linear curve (visualOffProgress = rawOffProgress^2.4) so the thumb visibly lags behind the pointer — real drag distance, small visual response — and only commits OFF once the raw drag has covered 85% of the travel, at which point a heavier, slower spring (k=55, zeta=1.05) finishes the release from wherever the sub-linear curve left it (a real, visible distance, not a snap from zero). Releasing before either coercive point relaxes the thumb back along whichever branch it was on (a light spring back to the anchor it started from) with no state change. A plain click always turns OFF->ON instantly (the cheap direction needs no ceremony), but a click while already ON does not turn it off — it only ARMS the intent, rendering a transient text badge ('Armed — drag the thumb to confirm off', 3s lifetime, role=status) with no aria-checked change; the OFF transition still requires a completed drag. Keyboard parity: Space when unchecked commits ON immediately; Space when checked arms a 3-second confirm window and an aria-live=polite paragraph (also the switch's aria-describedby target) swaps its text to 'Press Enter to confirm turning off.'; a confirming Enter within the window commits OFF (heavy spring), Escape or the 3s timeout or a blur cancels the window and the paragraph reverts to its resting description of the asymmetry. Direct-DOM refs drive the drag and spring hot path (pointer capture on pointerdown, position read from getBoundingClientRect each pointermove, thumb moved via style.transform only); React state holds only checked, the armed badge, and the confirm-pending flag. prefers-reduced-motion drops both springs and the relax animation — commits and relaxes land as instant discrete steps — while the 40%/85% thresholds and the sub-linear OFF mapping (a positional curve, not a timed animation) still apply. Colors are --foreground/--background/--border/--ns-muted only, with --ns-accent reserved for the focus-visible ring; the thumb fills solid --foreground when ON and sits hollow (--background fill, --foreground/70 stroke) when OFF, so the state reads without relying on color alone.
